paragraphs.title: Building the bronze altar and its utensils

easy.question: What were the length and width of the altar?
answers: Five cubits long and five cubits wide
Three cubits long and three cubits wide
Five cubits long and three cubits wide
easy.explanation: The verse says that the altar was five cubits long and five cubits wide.

easy.question: What material covered the altar?
answers: Gold
Brass
Silver
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt overlay it with brass.”

easy.question: Where were the horns of the altar?
answers: On only one side
In the middle of the altar
On its four corners
easy.explanation: The horns were placed on the altar’s four corners.

medium.question: What can we infer from the altar’s length and width being equal?
answers: Its base was square
The altar was round
The altar was taller than it was long
medium.explanation: Because the length and width were equal, and the altar was to be foursquare, its base was square.

medium.question: In the phrase “pans to receive his ashes,” what was the purpose of the pans?
answers: To decorate the altar
To remove the ashes
To measure the altar
medium.explanation: The pans were used to collect and remove the ashes from the altar.

medium.question: What is said about all the altar’s vessels after the different utensils are listed?
answers: They would all be made of wood
They would all be made of gold
They would all be made of brass
medium.explanation: The verse says that all the altar’s vessels were to be made of brass.

challenge.question: Which conclusion correctly describes the altar’s shape and dimensions?
answers: It had a square base and was three cubits high
It was a cube five cubits high
It had a rectangular base and was five cubits high
challenge.explanation: Its length and width were five cubits, making the base square; its height was three cubits.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “his horns shall be of the same” emphasize?
answers: The horns were made of another material
The horns were part of the altar itself
The horns were merely outside decorations
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the horns were part of the altar itself, not separate pieces added to it.

challenge.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between the altar and its vessels?
answers: The altar was made of gold and its vessels of wood
The altar was made of stone and its vessels of silver
The altar was made of shittim wood overlaid with brass, and its vessels were made of brass
challenge.explanation: The altar was made of shittim wood and overlaid with brass, while its vessels were also made of brass.

questions.question: Which conclusion correctly describes the altar’s shape and dimensions?
answers: It had a square base and was three cubits high
It was a cube five cubits high
It had a rectangular base and was five cubits high
questions.explanation: Its length and width were five cubits, making the base square; its height was three cubits.

questions.question: What does the phrase “his horns shall be of the same” emphasize?
answers: The horns were made of another material
The horns were part of the altar itself
The horns were merely outside decorations
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the horns were part of the altar itself, not separate pieces added to it.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between the altar and its vessels?
answers: The altar was made of gold and its vessels of wood
The altar was made of stone and its vessels of silver
The altar was made of shittim wood overlaid with brass, and its vessels were made of brass
questions.explanation: The altar was made of shittim wood and overlaid with brass, while its vessels were also made of brass.

paragraphs.title: The altar’s grate and carrying staves

easy.question: What material was used to make the altar’s grate?
answers: Brass
Gold
Wood
easy.explanation: The verse describes it as a grate of network made of brass.

easy.question: How many brass rings were to be made on the grate?
answers: Two rings
Four rings
Eight rings
easy.explanation: Four brass rings were to be made, one at each corner.

easy.question: What were the altar’s staves made of, and what covered them?
answers: Gold covered with silver
Brass covered with gold
Shittim wood covered with brass
easy.explanation: The staves were made of shittim wood and overlaid with brass.

medium.question: Where was the grate placed in relation to the altar, and how far did it reach?
answers: Above the compass and up to the top
Under the compass and halfway up the altar
Inside the altar and down to its bottom
medium.explanation: The grate was placed beneath the compass and reached halfway up the altar.

medium.question: In the phrase “hollow with boards shalt thou make it,” what does “hollow with boards” mean?
answers: Made from one solid block
Made from folded cloth
Hollow and made from boards
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the altar was hollow and constructed from boards rather than being solid.

medium.question: Why were the altar’s staves placed in the rings and along its two sides?
answers: So the altar could be carried
To decorate the altar
To attach the grate to the altar
medium.explanation: The staves were placed there so that the altar could be carried.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the altar having staves inserted into rings?
answers: The altar was designed to be portable
The altar was meant to remain fixed to the ground
The altar was mainly used as a storage place
challenge.explanation: The rings and staves were carrying equipment, showing that the altar was meant to be moved.

challenge.question: What does the instruction “as it was shewed thee in the mount, so shall they make it” teach?
answers: The altar could be changed as needed
The altar had to be built according to the model shown to Moses on the mount
The altar was built only after entering the land
challenge.explanation: The instruction requires the altar to be made according to what God showed Moses on the mount.

challenge.question: What is distinctive about the grate’s location according to these verses?
answers: It covered the entire top of the altar
It stood outside the altar without being attached
It was under the compass and reached only halfway up the altar
challenge.explanation: The verses specify both that it was under the compass and that it reached only to the middle of the altar.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the altar having staves inserted into rings?
answers: The altar was designed to be portable
The altar was meant to remain fixed to the ground
The altar was mainly used as a storage place
questions.explanation: The rings and staves were carrying equipment, showing that the altar was meant to be moved.

questions.question: What does the instruction “as it was shewed thee in the mount, so shall they make it” teach?
answers: The altar could be changed as needed
The altar had to be built according to the model shown to Moses on the mount
The altar was built only after entering the land
questions.explanation: The instruction requires the altar to be made according to what God showed Moses on the mount.

questions.question: What is distinctive about the grate’s location according to these verses?
answers: It covered the entire top of the altar
It stood outside the altar without being attached
It was under the compass and reached only halfway up the altar
questions.explanation: The verses specify both that it was under the compass and that it reached only to the middle of the altar.

paragraphs.title: The south and north court hangings

easy.question: How long were the hangings on the south side of the court?
answers: One hundred cubits
Twenty cubits
Fifty cubits
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that the hangings on the south side were one hundred cubits long.

easy.question: How many pillars were on the south side?
answers: Ten
Twenty
Thirty
easy.explanation: Verse 10 says that there were twenty pillars.

easy.question: What material were the pillars’ hooks and fillets made of?
answers: Brass
Gold
Silver
easy.explanation: The verse says that the hooks and fillets were made of silver.

medium.question: What can we understand from the north side repeating almost the same details as the south side?
answers: The two sides had a similar design
Only the north side had hangings
The north side was shorter
medium.explanation: Both sides had hangings one hundred cubits long, twenty pillars, and twenty sockets.

medium.question: In the phrase “for the south side southward,” what does the phrase identify?
answers: The material used
The side or section of the court
The entrance
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies a particular side or section of the court.

medium.question: Which detail was shared by the south and north sides?
answers: Both had ten pillars
Both had silver sockets
Both had hangings one hundred cubits long
medium.explanation: The hangings on both sides were one hundred cubits long.

challenge.question: Which word in verse 11 emphasizes that the north side followed the pattern already described?
answers: “Likewise”
“In length”
“Brass”
challenge.explanation: “Likewise” shows that the north side was made in the same way as the south side.

challenge.question: Which combination correctly matches the court’s parts?
answers: Silver pillars and brass sockets
Pillars with silver hooks and brass sockets
Gold pillars and silver sockets
challenge.explanation: The verses mention brass sockets, while the pillars’ hooks and fillets were silver.

challenge.question: Why can’t the entire perimeter of the court be calculated from verses 9–11 alone?
answers: The length of the hangings is not given
The number of pillars is not given
Only the south and north sides are described
challenge.explanation: The verses describe only two sides, leaving out the east and west sides.

questions.question: Which word in verse 11 emphasizes that the north side followed the pattern already described?
answers: “Likewise”
“In length”
“Brass”
questions.explanation: “Likewise” shows that the north side was made in the same way as the south side.

questions.question: Which combination correctly matches the court’s parts?
answers: Silver pillars and brass sockets
Pillars with silver hooks and brass sockets
Gold pillars and silver sockets
questions.explanation: The verses mention brass sockets, while the pillars’ hooks and fillets were silver.

questions.question: Why can’t the entire perimeter of the court be calculated from verses 9–11 alone?
answers: The length of the hangings is not given
The number of pillars is not given
Only the south and north sides are described
questions.explanation: The verses describe only two sides, leaving out the east and west sides.

paragraphs.title: The court’s width and entrance gate

easy.question: What was the width of the court on the west side?
answers: Fifty cubits
Twenty cubits
Fifteen cubits
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that the hangings on the west side were fifty cubits wide.

easy.question: What was the width of the court on the east side?
answers: Twenty cubits
Fifty cubits
Thirty cubits
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says that the east side was fifty cubits wide.

easy.question: How wide was the hanging at the court gate?
answers: Fifteen cubits
Fifty cubits
Twenty cubits
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says that the gate hanging was twenty cubits wide.

medium.question: What was the total width of the hangings on the two sides of the gate, excluding the gate itself?
answers: Thirty cubits
Twenty cubits
Fifty cubits
medium.explanation: Each side had fifteen cubits of hangings, making thirty cubits altogether.

medium.question: In the phrase “for the gate of the court shall be an hanging,” what was the hanging?
answers: A tall pillar
A curtain or covering
A pillar base
medium.explanation: The hanging was a curtain or covering placed at the entrance.

medium.question: By how many cubits was the court gate wider than the hanging on each side of it?
answers: Ten cubits
Twenty cubits
Five cubits
medium.explanation: The gate was twenty cubits wide, while each side hanging was fifteen cubits wide, a difference of five cubits.

challenge.question: How does the east side add up to fifty cubits when the gate and side hangings are included?
answers: 15 cubits + 20 cubits + 15 cubits
20 cubits + 20 cubits + 20 cubits
50 cubits + 15 cubits
challenge.explanation: The east side consisted of fifteen cubits of hanging, a twenty-cubit gate, and another fifteen cubits of hanging.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the descriptions of the west and east sides?
answers: Only the west had pillars
The east includes a central gate, while the west is described only by the length of its hangings
The east had no hangings at all
challenge.explanation: Both sides were fifty cubits wide, but the east side is described as two hangings with a gate between them.

challenge.question: What special detail is given about the court gate hanging compared with the side hangings?
answers: It was made of stone
It had only two pillars
It was embroidered and made with several colors
challenge.explanation: The gate hanging was made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, with needlework.

questions.question: How does the east side add up to fifty cubits when the gate and side hangings are included?
answers: 15 cubits + 20 cubits + 15 cubits
20 cubits + 20 cubits + 20 cubits
50 cubits + 15 cubits
questions.explanation: The east side consisted of fifteen cubits of hanging, a twenty-cubit gate, and another fifteen cubits of hanging.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the descriptions of the west and east sides?
answers: Only the west had pillars
The east includes a central gate, while the west is described only by the length of its hangings
The east had no hangings at all
questions.explanation: Both sides were fifty cubits wide, but the east side is described as two hangings with a gate between them.

questions.question: What special detail is given about the court gate hanging compared with the side hangings?
answers: It was made of stone
It had only two pillars
It was embroidered and made with several colors
questions.explanation: The gate hanging was made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, with needlework.

paragraphs.title: The court’s structure and bronze equipment

easy.question: What material surrounded or connected the court pillars?
answers: Silver
Brass
Gold
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says that all the court pillars were filleted with silver.

easy.question: What was the length of the court?
answers: Fifty cubits
One hundred cubits
Five cubits
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says that the court was one hundred cubits long.

easy.question: What material were the court pins made of?
answers: Silver
Fine twined linen
Brass
easy.explanation: Verse 19 says that the pins of the court were made of brass.

medium.question: What material was used for both the pillar sockets and the court pins?
answers: Brass
Silver
Fine twined linen
medium.explanation: The verses identify both the sockets and the pins as being made of brass.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the pillars round about the court shall be filleted with silver,” what does “filleted” mean?
answers: Covered with cloth
Connected or surrounded with silver bands
Made of brass
medium.explanation: The word describes the pillars as being connected or surrounded by silver fittings.

medium.question: What is described in order in verses 17–19?
answers: The pins, then the sockets, and finally the court’s dimensions
The court’s dimensions, then the pillars, and finally the tabernacle vessels
The pillars and their fittings, then the court’s dimensions, and finally the vessels and pins
medium.explanation: Verse 17 describes the pillars and fittings, verse 18 gives the court’s dimensions, and verse 19 lists the equipment and pins.

challenge.question: What was the ratio of the court’s length to its width?
answers: The length was twice the width
The length equaled the width
The length was half the width
challenge.explanation: The court was one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, so its length was twice its width.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from verse 19 listing the tabernacle vessels, the pins, and the court pins?
answers: Only the pillars were important to the court’s construction
The command included the equipment and smaller parts needed for the tabernacle’s service
All the equipment was made only of silver
challenge.explanation: The verse includes not only the structure but also the vessels and pins needed for use and stability.

challenge.question: What difference in materials stands out among the court’s parts?
answers: The pillars and sockets were all silver
The pillars were brass and the sockets silver
The pillar fittings were silver, while the sockets and pins were brass
challenge.explanation: The verses specify silver for the pillar fittings and hooks, and brass for the sockets and pins.

questions.question: What was the ratio of the court’s length to its width?
answers: The length was twice the width
The length equaled the width
The length was half the width
questions.explanation: The court was one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, so its length was twice its width.

questions.question: What can be inferred from verse 19 listing the tabernacle vessels, the pins, and the court pins?
answers: Only the pillars were important to the court’s construction
The command included the equipment and smaller parts needed for the tabernacle’s service
All the equipment was made only of silver
questions.explanation: The verse includes not only the structure but also the vessels and pins needed for use and stability.

questions.question: What difference in materials stands out among the court’s parts?
answers: The pillars and sockets were all silver
The pillars were brass and the sockets silver
The pillar fittings were silver, while the sockets and pins were brass
questions.explanation: The verses specify silver for the pillar fittings and hooks, and brass for the sockets and pins.

paragraphs.title: Olive oil for the perpetual light

easy.question: To whom is the command in this verse addressed?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The words “thou shalt command” are addressed to Moses.

easy.question: What were the children of Israel to bring?
answers: Fish oil
Pure olive oil
Pure water
easy.explanation: The verse says that they were to bring pure olive oil.

easy.question: What was the oil intended for?
answers: Anointing the priests
Preparing offerings
Keeping the lamp burning
easy.explanation: The oil was for the light, so that the lamp would burn continually.

medium.question: What sequence of actions is described in the verse?
answers: The Israelites bring oil so that the lamp can burn
Moses brings water to wash the lamp
Aaron brings incense to light the altar
medium.explanation: First the Israelites are told to bring oil, and then it is used to keep the lamp burning.

medium.question: In the phrase “to cause the lamp to burn always,” what does “always” emphasize?
answers: Only in the morning
Continually and without interruption
Only once
medium.explanation: “Always” indicates that the light was to be maintained continually.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites commanded to bring pure olive oil?
answers: So they would have oil for food
So they could anoint Moses
So there would be suitable fuel for the light
medium.explanation: The oil was intended for the light, so it had to be pure olive oil suitable for burning.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “bring thee pure olive oil” show about the oil?
answers: It was to be brought to Moses
It was to be poured directly onto the lamp
It was to be taken outside the camp
challenge.explanation: The wording identifies Moses as the recipient to whom the Israelites were to bring the oil.

challenge.question: What idea is especially emphasized by the word “always”?
answers: The lamp had to be large
The light had to be maintained continually
The oil had to be colorful
challenge.explanation: The word refers to the continuing duration of the light, not the lamp’s size or the oil’s color.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “pure olive oil beaten”?
answers: It was oil mixed with water
It was oil intended mainly for eating
It was clean olive oil produced by pressing or crushing
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes pure oil extracted from olives and suitable for use as lamp oil.

questions.question: What does the phrase “bring thee pure olive oil” show about the oil?
answers: It was to be brought to Moses
It was to be poured directly onto the lamp
It was to be taken outside the camp
questions.explanation: The wording identifies Moses as the recipient to whom the Israelites were to bring the oil.

questions.question: What idea is especially emphasized by the word “always”?
answers: The lamp had to be large
The light had to be maintained continually
The oil had to be colorful
questions.explanation: The word refers to the continuing duration of the light, not the lamp’s size or the oil’s color.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “pure olive oil beaten”?
answers: It was oil mixed with water
It was oil intended mainly for eating
It was clean olive oil produced by pressing or crushing
questions.explanation: The phrase describes pure oil extracted from olives and suitable for use as lamp oil.

paragraphs.title: Tending the lamp before the Lord

easy.question: Who was commanded to tend the lamp?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses and his sons
The entire nation
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Aaron and his sons would tend it.

easy.question: When was the lamp to be tended?
answers: Only in the morning
From evening until morning
Only at noon
easy.explanation: The verse says that it was to be tended from evening until morning.

easy.question: Where was this work to be performed?
answers: In the court of the tabernacle
Outside the camp
In the tabernacle, outside the veil
easy.explanation: The verse places the work in the tabernacle, outside the veil before the testimony.

medium.question: What can we understand from the command to tend the lamp “from evening until morning”?
answers: The lamp was intended to burn during the night
The lamp was lit only during travel
The lamp was used only during the daytime
medium.explanation: The time period from evening until morning shows that the lamp was to burn through the night.

medium.question: In the phrase “without the vail, which is before the testimony,” what does the veil do?
answers: It serves as an altar for sacrifices
It is a vessel for lighting the lamp
It separates different areas of the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The veil was a screen separating areas within the tabernacle.

medium.question: What does “on the behalf of the children of Israel” show about the people’s role?
answers: The people supplied what was needed for the holy service
The people replaced Aaron in his duties
The people entered the tabernacle every night
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the Israelites provided what was needed, while Aaron and his sons performed the service.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “before the Lord,” even though the lamp was outside the veil?
answers: The work was unrelated to the sanctuary
The veil was outside the tabernacle
The place was still part of the sacred service before the Lord
challenge.explanation: Although the lamp was outside the veil, it was still inside the tabernacle and part of the holy service before the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “a statute for ever unto their generations” mean about this command?
answers: It was a one-time command
It was a law intended to continue through the generations
It was a custom only for Aaron
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the command was not limited to one generation but was to continue forever.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that tending the lamp was a regular, ongoing practice?
answers: The words “from evening until morning”
The mention of the children of Israel alone
The location outside the veil alone
challenge.explanation: The precise time period shows that this was a regular nightly duty.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the words “before the Lord,” even though the lamp was outside the veil?
answers: The work was unrelated to the sanctuary
The veil was outside the tabernacle
The place was still part of the sacred service before the Lord
questions.explanation: Although the lamp was outside the veil, it was still inside the tabernacle and part of the holy service before the Lord.

questions.question: What does “a statute for ever unto their generations” mean about this command?
answers: It was a one-time command
It was a law intended to continue through the generations
It was a custom only for Aaron
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the command was not limited to one generation but was to continue forever.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that tending the lamp was a regular, ongoing practice?
answers: The words “from evening until morning”
The mention of the children of Israel alone
The location outside the veil alone
questions.explanation: The precise time period shows that this was a regular nightly duty.
